query: For boride-based components used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment, what single intervention could improve resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, defines the conditions under which it should remain effective, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment whose results could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a controlled amount of molybdenum (Mo) to boride‐based components improves resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion by promoting the formation of a protective, Mo-enriched passivating surface layer.
generation.material_initial_state: Standard boride-based component without Mo modification
generation.intervention: Alloying the boride-based component with a small, optimized concentration of Mo
generation.conditions: Exposure to molten aluminum under temperatures and durations typical in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a Mo-rich surface layer (or Mo-containing borides) that enhances the continuous, protective oxide/boride scale on the component
generation.mechanism: Molybdenum is known to improve passivation capacity, thereby facilitating the formation of a stable, protective surface layer that reduces direct contact between the molten aluminum and the underlying component, mitigating corrosion. This mechanism is analogous to observations in high-temperature alloys where Mo promotes better surface passivation.
generation.predicted_outcome: A measurable reduction in corrosion rate (e.g., lower corrosion current density and weight loss over time) relative to components without Mo, as well as improved integrity of the protective surface layer during molten aluminum exposure
generation.baseline: Boride-based components made without Mo addition
generation.boundary: The improvement is expected when the Mo concentration is within an optimal range; concentrations outside this range or under significantly different process temperatures may not yield the desired effect. Long-term phase stability under cyclic or extreme conditions remains to be validated.
generation.uncertainty: The optimal Mo concentration and the long-term stability of the Mo-enriched passivating layer under continuous molten aluminum exposure are uncertain and require further experimental calibration.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two groups of boride-based components: one set with the standard composition and another set with a controlled Mo addition. Subject both groups to identical hot-dip aluminum-plating conditions by immersing them in molten aluminum. Monitor the exposure over a set duration, replicating industrial conditions.
measurements: Weight loss before and after exposure
Microscopic analysis (e.g., SEM) of surface morphology
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Mo-alloyed samples do not exhibit statistically significant improvements in corrosion resistance metrics (i.e., similar or higher corrosion current densities and weight loss, or reveal deleterious phase formation compared to the control group), then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: It was found that, by reducing the Mn concentration (to 5 at.% Mn), the CoCrFeMnNi alloy acquires higher yield strength values after annealing at 1117 K (from 387 to 477 MPa) due to the grain refinement effect (from 4.4 to 2.61 µm) []. Mn also shows a rapid evaporation effect during melting processes; hence, in our study, this element was replaced by Mo, which could improve the resistance to high temperatures []. Co–Cr–Mo alloy is widely used for manufacturing of vanes and gas turbines due to its excellent fatigue behavior and wear resistance [,,,]. In such alloys, molybdenum has a beneficial effect on passivation capacity, contributing to the formation of a protective surface layer that allows pitting corrosion to be limited [,]. Studies were conducted to estimate the effects on the microstructure and properties of alloys with different Mo contents [,,]. Such alloys have been designed for the manufacture of furnace casings and chemical tanks used in high-temperature and corrosion conditions [], for components used in the geothermal industry [,], or to obtain high-performance coatings [].
